edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 29 September 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 30 September 2026

items.caseName: Assistant Commissioner v. Shruti Gupta & Ors
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Missed 30-day window: Customs' bank guarantees fall into liquidation estate
items.text: The appellate tribunal ruled that a secured creditor which does not communicate its choice on its security interest within 30 days of liquidation commencement is treated as having relinquished it under Regulation 21A of the Liquidation Regulations. The Customs Department's later decision to retain bank guarantees could not cure the lapse, so the guarantees and fixed deposits formed part of the estate and Customs ranks under the Section 53 waterfall.

items.caseName: Dr. Subhash Chandra (Personal Guarantor) v. Shiv Nandan Sharma (Resolution Professional)
items.coram: Justice Yogesh Khanna (Officiating Chairperson), Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra (Technical Members)
items.headline: Notice issued on Subhash Chandra's challenge to asset-alienation curb
items.text: The NCLAT issued notice on the personal guarantor's appeals against the NCLT's 1 September 2026 order barring him from transferring assets while his ₹6.25 crore repayment plan, set against claims of about ₹22,006 crore, is in force. The Solicitor General sought a later date citing maintainability concerns and linkage with creditors' appeals listed on 7 October; the matter is next listed on 29–30 October 2026.

items.caseName: Eastern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited v. Daulat Resolution Services Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Litigant not to suffer for counsel's deliberate absence; ₹20.72 crore power-dues claim revived
items.text: The tribunal restored a discom's ₹20.72 crore electricity dues application that had been dismissed for non-prosecution, finding the earlier lawyer had deliberately stopped appearing and withheld a no-objection for substitution. Distinguishing such conduct from ordinary negligence, it relied on Rafiq v. Munshilal and used Section 238A IBC with Section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone the delay, sending the claim back for decision on merits.

items.caseName: Vijaybhai Dhanjibhai Detroja v. Vidres India Ceramics Private Limited & Anr
items.coram: Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member) and Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: Post-admission settlement no ground to quash CIRP; Section 12A route must be used
items.text: Although the operational creditor had settled with the corporate debtor after admission and consented to closure, the appellate tribunal declined to set aside the Section 9 admission order itself. It said the settlement is a relevant development but cannot bypass the statutory withdrawal scheme, and directed the IRP to move the NCLT under Section 12A.

items.caseName: Jayanti Lal Jain, IRP of DK Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. Arvind Mathur & Ors
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) and Charanjeet Singh Gulati (Technical Member)
items.headline: Bank guarantee can be encashed during CIRP moratorium
items.text: The Mumbai bench held that invoking a bank guarantee furnished on the corporate debtor's behalf does not breach the Section 14 moratorium, as such guarantees fall within the Section 14(3)(b) carve-out for sureties. Encashment is enforcement against the bank's own undertaking, not against the debtor's assets.

items.caseName: Shailendra Kataria, Authorised Representative of Creditors in Class (Homebuyers) v. Manish Lalji Dawda, Resolution Professional of Wadhwa Buildcon LLP
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) and Charanjeet Singh Gulati (Technical Member)
items.headline: Replacement RP may re-verify claims admitted by predecessor
items.text: Rejecting the homebuyers' challenge, the tribunal held that a new resolution professional may re-examine claims admitted earlier where records show gaps or doubts over authenticity, as part of the duty to keep the creditor list current under Section 25(2)(e) and Regulation 13. In the Wadhwa Buildcon matter, the re-verification cut the homebuyers' voting share from about 66% to about 30%.

items.caseName: Button Industries Pvt Ltd vs Viaz Tyres Limited
items.coram: Chitra Hanakre (Judicial Member) and Dr VG Venakata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Rescheduled supply dues remain operational debt; Section 7 plea rejected
items.text: The bench dismissed a financial-creditor petition over ₹1.16 crore, holding that dues arising from rice supply invoices kept their operational character even after MoUs rescheduled repayment. Since no fresh money was disbursed against the time value of money, the debt did not meet the Section 5(8) definition of financial debt.

items.caseName: Agrirevolve Trading Private Limited v. Spright Agro Limited
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr VG Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Spright Agro admitted to CIRP over ₹8.66 crore supply dues
items.text: The tribunal admitted the operational creditor's petition, finding debt and default proved through authenticated NeSL records. The debtor only contested the 18% contractual interest, but the principal alone crossed the statutory threshold; an IRP was appointed and moratorium declared.

items.caseName: Magnum Ventures Limited vs Magnum Paperz Limited
items.coram: Praveen Gupta (Judicial Member) and Ashish Verma (Technical Member)
items.headline: First-motion nod for demerger of Magnum Ventures' paper business
items.text: The Allahabad bench allowed the first-motion application to hive off Magnum Ventures' paper manufacturing unit into Magnum Paperz, with the hospitality business staying with the parent. It ordered meetings of equity shareholders, debenture holders and creditors on 20 November 2026 by video conference with e-voting, and dispensed with other meetings on unanimous consent.

items.caseName: I-NXT v. Sandeep Banga, Commissioner, Bengaluru Zone & Ors.
items.coram: Sudha Koka (Technical Member) and Srikanth Venkatraman (Judicial Member)
items.headline: GSTR-3B/2A mismatch alone cannot justify 100% Section 74 penalty
items.text: The Bengaluru bench struck down a full penalty under Section 74 CGST Act, saying the department must link excess ITC to fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression rather than merely reciting the statutory words. The taxpayer had already repaid about ₹2.74 crore of excess credit with interest.

items.caseName: DGAP, DG Anti Profiteering, Director General of Anti-Profiteering v. Vertex Homes Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Anil Kumar Gupta (Technical Member)
items.headline: Cost escalation offsets ITC gain; no profiteering by Vertex Homes
items.text: The tribunal closed anti-profiteering proceedings against the developer after accepting DGAP's revised finding that a ₹3.49 crore rise in construction costs outweighed the ₹2.47 crore additional ITC benefit. Relying on Reckitt Benckiser, it held genuine cost increases can be set off when computing profiteering under Section 171.

items.caseName: Sri Kamalaganapathy Steel Rolling Mills Ltd. v. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise and Shri C. Saravanan v. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise
items.coram: P. Dinesha (Judicial Member) and M. Ajit Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Uncertified electronic data cannot fix excise liability
items.text: The tribunal ruled that seized electronic records and printouts are inadmissible to prove clandestine clearance unless Section 36B of the Central Excise Act is complied with. It partly set aside a ₹4.08 crore demand and remanded it for re-quantification using only admissible documentary and circumstantial evidence.

items.caseName: DCIT, Central Circle-6 v. Sahara Airlines Ltd. (now known as Jet Lite (India) Ltd.) and connected appeals
items.coram: Anubhav Sharma (Judicial Member) and S Rifaur Rahman (Accountant Member)
items.headline: Revenue's decade-old appeals against Sahara Airlines fall with CIRP
items.text: The Delhi bench dismissed departmental appeals for assessment years 1998-99 to 2007-08, noting nothing showed the tax claims had been admitted in the airline's resolution or liquidation proceedings. With the claims extinguished through insolvency, the merits no longer needed examination.

edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 28 September 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 29 September 2026

items.caseName: Nikhil Rai & Ors v. VCare Technologies Private Limited & Ors
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Restructuring need no excuse to skip oppression inquiry
items.text: The appellate tribunal set aside the Delhi NCLT's dismissal of an oppression and mismanagement petition, saying a company's commercial need to restructure does not relieve the NCLT of its duty to examine such complaints. It found the NCLT had not recorded findings on asset transfers, debt conversion and shareholding dilution, and had denied the petitioners a fair chance to answer perjury allegations. The case goes back for fresh hearing, with status quo on shares and assets meanwhile.

items.caseName: Mrs V Lakshmi
items.coram: Jyoti Kumar Tripathi (Judicial Member), Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Guarantor insolvency not tied to company's default threshold
items.text: A personal guarantor who had backed Tamilnad Mercantile Bank loans to three companies applied for her own insolvency resolution under Section 94. The bank objected that the companies' defaults were below the corporate insolvency threshold, but the Chennai bench held that this does not block personal insolvency proceedings against the guarantor, and admitted her application.

items.caseName: Equentia Financial Service Pvt. Ltd. v. Saloni Ayush Aggarwal
items.coram: Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj (Judicial Member), Atul Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: 2026 amendment on guarantor moratorium applies to pending cases
items.text: Three personal guarantors of Prafful Overseas argued that a creditor's insolvency applications were barred by the interim moratorium under Section 96, since a Canara Bank case was already pending against them in Ahmedabad. The Delhi bench ruled that the 2026 amendment removing that protection for personal guarantors covers pending matters too, and admitted all three applications.

items.caseName: Mukesh Goyal v. CA Santanu Brahma & Ors.
items.coram: Rekha Kantilal Shah (Technical Member), Labh Singh (Judicial Member)
items.headline: Plan clause extends timeline after appeal, no fresh nod needed
items.text: The successful resolution applicant for Aanchal Ispat asked for its implementation deadlines to be recalculated after it had successfully challenged some observations in the approval order before the NCLAT. The Kolkata bench held that the plan's own clause excluding time lost to appeals kicks in automatically, without a stay order or fresh approval from the CoC or the tribunal, and told the monitoring committee to redo the schedule.

items.caseName: Think & Learn Pvt Ltd v. Aakash Educational Services Ltd and Others
items.coram: Sunil Kumar Aggarwal (Judicial Member), Radhakrishna Sreepada (Technical Member)
items.headline: Byju's-Aakash settlement: NCLT wants RP's consent on record first
items.text: Byju's parent and Aakash jointly asked the Bengaluru bench to close their rights-issue dispute on the basis of a settlement. The bench held off, asking for the original power of attorney used by the resolution professional's counsel, written proof of the RP's consent, an affidavit that the deal complies with pending court orders and contracts, and filings withdrawing claims against the other respondents.

items.caseName: DGAP, DG Anti Profiteering, Director General of Anti-Profiteering v. Bengal Emami Housing Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Sanjaya Kumar Mishra (President), Anil Kumar Gupta (Technical Member)
items.headline: Bengal Emami told to pass ₹70.58 lakh ITC benefit to HIG buyers
items.text: In an anti-profiteering case over the Swan Court project in Kolkata, the tribunal accepted that LIG and MIG flat prices were fixed by state notification and limited the calculation to HIG units. It directed the developer to pay ₹70.58 lakh with 18% annual interest to eligible HIG buyers. A 10% penalty will be waived if the full refund is made within 30 days.

items.caseName: Amit Tyagi v. Tata Play Limited, Managing Director & CEO
items.coram: Ajeet Singh (Judicial Member), Vivek Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Split verdict on Tata Play e-way bill penalty goes to VP
items.text: A Tata Play consignment was stopped with an e-way bill carrying a completely different vehicle number, drawing a ₹10.10 lakh penalty under Section 129 that was later deleted. On the State's appeal, the judicial member held the CBIC relief covers only one- or two-digit errors, while the technical member found no sign of tax evasion. The matter has been sent to the GSTAT Vice President.

items.caseName: R R Infrastructure Projects v. Shashi Bhushan Singh, Additional Commissioner, Grade II Appeal & Ors.
items.coram: Narendra Kumar (Judicial Member), Alok Chopra (Technical Member)
items.headline: GSTR-3B vs 2A mismatch alone can't sink ITC claim
items.text: The department demanded about ₹6.35 lakh for 2017-18 because the ITC claimed in GSTR-3B was higher than what showed in GSTR-2A. The Lucknow bench held that the whole gap cannot be treated as ineligible credit without checking reconciliation and supporting documents, and sent the case back for invoice-wise verification in line with CBIC Circular 183/15/2022-GST.

items.caseName: DGAP, DG Anti Profiteering, Director General of Anti-Profiteering v. Devi 70MM
items.coram: Justice Mayank Kumar Jain (Single Member)
items.headline: Hyderabad cinema must deposit ₹81,722 for keeping rate cut
items.text: When GST on cinema tickets up to ₹100 fell from 18% to 12% in January 2019, the Devi 70MM theatre kept ticket prices the same by raising the base price. The tribunal rejected arguments about film demand and holidays, and directed a deposit of ₹81,722 with 18% interest, split between the central and Telangana consumer welfare funds. No penalty was imposed.

items.caseName: Sarda Energy and Minerals Ltd. v. Commissioner (Appeal), CGST, Central Excise and Customs
items.coram: Somesh Arora (Judicial Member), Sanjiv Srivastava (Technical Member)
items.headline: Exporter not liable for reverse-charge tax on foreign bank fees
items.text: The department sought about ₹1.88 lakh in service tax from an exporter under reverse charge on commissions and charges levied by foreign banks. CESTAT held that the exporter had no contract with the foreign banks, so the Indian bank that dealt with them was the service recipient. The demand and penalties were set aside, and the extended limitation period was also held not to apply.

edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 27 September 2026 and 11:15 AM IST on 28 September 2026, plus four NCLT rulings reported on 26 September that were not carried earlier

items.caseName: Uber Health Tech Private Limited v. The Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax
items.coram: Prashant Maharishi (Vice President) & Soundararajan K. (Judicial Member)
items.headline: Corrected 'defective' return dates back to original filing
items.text: The bench held that a return corrected under Section 139(9) within the permitted time is treated as filed on the original date, not as a fresh return. Measured from that date, the Section 143(2) scrutiny notice of 22 September 2019 was issued after the 30 September 2018 limit. The assessment and the ₹6.39 crore addition under Section 68 were set aside. The order is dated 21 September 2026.

items.caseName: Alliance Advertising and Marketing Pvt. Ltd. v. Eduisfun Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Nilesh Sharma (Judicial Member) & Sameer Kakar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Tribunal will not rebuild a creditor's defective petition
items.text: The operational creditor declined to amend its petition, and the bench said it cannot itself split invoices or recompute the default to save the case. Defaults falling in the Section 10A COVID-19 period could not found the petition, and interest was claimed without any contractual basis. The insolvency petition was dismissed.

items.caseName: Prafull Sawant (Applicant), in the matter of Becchu Tiwari
items.caseNo: Company Application No. 67 of 2021 in CP (IB) 277 of 2018
items.coram: Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey (Judicial Member) & Prabhat Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Attachment lifted on properties of two ex-PNB officers
items.text: Two Punjab National Bank officers named in proceedings linked to the Nirav Modi–Mehul Choksi group fraud sought release of their attached properties. The bench found the case against them rested mainly on circumstantial inferences, with no incriminating material from the SFIO, and vacated the attachment. It declined to drop them from the petition, holding that their role under Section 339 of the Companies Act must still be tested on evidence.

items.caseName: Sesa Care Private Limited v. Dabur India Limited
items.coram: Bachu Venkat Balaram Das (Judicial Member) & Ravindra Chaturvedi (Technical Member)
items.headline: Sesa Care–Dabur merger sanctioned
items.text: The bench sanctioned the scheme amalgamating Sesa Care into Dabur India with effect from 1 April 2026, after shareholders and creditors had approved it by large majorities. Having dealt with the observations of SEBI, the Regional Director and the Income Tax Department, it found the scheme fair and reasonable. The order is dated 24 September 2026.

items.caseName: In the matter of Scheme of Merger by Absorption between CIE Aluminium Casting India Limited and CIE Automotive India Limited
items.coram: K.R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) & Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: First-motion nod for CIE group merger
items.text: The bench allowed the first-motion application under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act for merging CIE Aluminium Casting into its parent, CIE Automotive India. Meetings of shareholders and creditors were dispensed with because the transferor is wholly owned and no compromise with creditors is involved. Notices must still go to shareholders, unsecured creditors and regulators, who have 30 days to respond.

edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 11:00 AM IST on 26 September 2026 and 3:30 PM IST on 27 September 2026

items.caseName: Punjab National Bank v. Reji Abraham
items.coram: Sanjiv Jain (Judicial Member) & Venkataraman Subramaniam (Technical Member)
items.headline: No IBC jurisdiction over guarantor of foreign borrowers
items.text: PNB sought personal insolvency proceedings against the guarantor of loans taken by three companies incorporated in Singapore and Norway. The bench said its territorial jurisdiction turns on where the corporate borrower's registered office is, and these borrowers had none in India. The Section 95 application was dismissed.

items.caseName: Indojewel Jewellery Private Limited v. Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) & Charanjeet Singh Gulati (Technical Member)
items.headline: BMC's property-tax charge survives liquidation sale
items.text: The buyer of a property in a liquidation auction argued that BMC's claim for unpaid property tax ended with the sale. The bench held that BMC's statutory first charge under the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act is not wiped out merely because BMC took part in the liquidation. Since the sale was on an 'as is where is' basis, the purchaser must bear dues of about ₹86.58 lakh.

items.caseName: S. Viswanathan v. Canara Bank
items.coram: Justice N. Seshasayee (Judicial Member) & Jatindranath Swain (Technical Member)
items.headline: CoC's call to replace the RP must be respected
items.text: The resolution professional of Maylari Agro Products challenged his replacement, voted for by Canara Bank with an 84.6% share. The appellate tribunal held that the CoC's commercial wisdom governs such a decision unless the RP is being asked to act against the Code. It dismissed the appeal but expunged adverse remarks and left his fee claim to the NCLT.

items.caseName: Hinduja National Power Corporation Limited & GOCL Corporation Limited v. The Regional Director & RoC
items.coram: Justice N. Seshasayee (Judicial Member) & Jatindranath Swain (Technical Member)
items.headline: Merger scheme wrongly rejected at first motion
items.text: NCLT Amravati had rejected the first-motion application for the merger of HNPCL with GOCL. The appellate tribunal held the NCLT stepped in too early, before shareholders and creditors had voted on the scheme. It directed the NCLT to convene the meetings by 5 October 2026, leaving objections for the second stage.

items.caseName: Odisha State Beverages Corporation Limited v. Commissioner of CGST and Central Excise
items.coram: R. Muralidhar (Judicial Member) & K. Anpazhakan (Technical Member)
items.headline: Licence fee paid to State is not payment for a service
items.text: The department sought service tax on licence fees the State beverages corporation paid to the Odisha government. The tribunal found the State did no separate activity for the corporation in return for the fee. Grant of a statutory licence alone does not create a service provider and recipient relationship under the Finance Act, 1994.

items.caseName: Oxonian India Foundation v. CIT (Exemptions)
items.coram: Raj Kumar Chauhan (Judicial Member) & Amitabh Shukla (Accountant Member)
items.headline: Scholarships for study abroad don't defeat charitable status
items.text: Registration was refused because the foundation's scholarships went to Indian students studying overseas. The tribunal held that scholarships paid in India are not income applied outside India just because the recipients study abroad. It directed the authority to grant registration under Section 12A and approval under Section 80G within four weeks.

items.caseName: Nandkishor Shantaram Kadam v. Income Tax Officer, Ward 42(2)(4), Mumbai
items.coram: SaktiJit Dey (Vice President) & G.M. Doss (Accountant Member)
items.headline: 10% stamp-duty tolerance band applies retrospectively
items.text: The property's price was about 6% below its stamp duty value, and the officer added the difference as income. The tribunal treated the 10% tolerance introduced by the Finance Act, 2020 as curative and retrospective. The addition of ₹3.77 lakh was deleted.

items.caseName: Dalbir Singh v. ITO, Ward 1
items.coram: Rajesh Damodarlal Sharma (Judicial Member) & Manoj Kumar Aggarwal (Accountant Member)
items.headline: Section 69 can't reach investments shown in the books
items.text: The assessee's ₹126.58 lakh property investment was recorded in his balance sheets across several years. The tribunal held that Section 69 applies only to unrecorded investments, and doubts about supporting documents do not turn a recorded investment into an unexplained one. The addition was deleted.

items.caseName: State Bank of India v. ACIT, TDS Circle 2(2)
items.coram: Pawan Singh (Judicial Member) & Om Prakash Kant (Accountant Member)
items.headline: SBI not in default for no TDS on LFC payments
items.text: SBI was held to be in default for not deducting tax on leave fare concession paid to employees whose travel included foreign legs, for AY 2016-17. The tribunal found the bank was under an obligation not to deduct tax at source in the circumstances. The appeal was allowed.

items.caseName: AT Kumar Minz v. B.L. Agro Industries Limited
items.coram: Santosh Kumar Srivastava (Judicial Member) & Arvind Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Amended refund formula in Rule 89(5) applies to pending claims
items.text: The edible-oil maker sought refunds of accumulated input tax credit under the inverted duty structure. The tribunal held the amendment to Rule 89(5) is curative and clarificatory and can apply to eligible claims filed within the two-year limit. All five appeals by the CGST department were dismissed.

items.caseName: Cent Bank Home Finance Ltd. v. Commissioner, State Tax, Chhattisgarh & Ors.
items.coram: Pradeep Kumar Vyas (Judicial Member) & Chandra Bhushan Singh (Technical Member)
items.headline: Recovery of loan amounts is an exempt supply
items.text: A GST demand of about ₹4.18 lakh was raised after the department disputed the exemption the housing finance company claimed. The tribunal treated recovery of loan amounts as exempt under Notification No. 12/2017. It found banking records on a written-off loan had not been properly examined and sent the matter back for fresh decision.

items.caseName: Partha Tribedi v. Vivek Ranjan
items.coram: S.G. Chattopadhyay (Judicial Member) & Bijoy Kumar Kar (Technical Member)
items.headline: No GST demand without a statutory show cause notice
items.text: After a search at a pan masala trader's premises, officials raised a demand without first serving a statutory show cause notice. The tribunal held that tax, interest and penalty can be demanded only after such a notice, and no other document can take its place. The Section 74 proceedings were quashed.

items.caseName: Union Bank of India v. SE Transstadia Private Limited
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) & Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: ₹223.82 crore insolvency plea admitted
items.text: The corporate debtor argued the bank's claim was time-barred. The bench held that revival letters of 2019, 2022 and 2025 were valid acknowledgments extending limitation, along with the COVID-period exclusion. It admitted the company into insolvency and appointed an interim resolution professional.

items.caseName: Mobligent Media Pvt. Ltd. v. SynergyByte Infotainment Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Khetrabasi Biswal (Judicial Member) & Shishir Agarwal (Technical Member)
items.headline: CIRP admitted over unpaid marketing invoices
items.text: The operational creditor claimed about ₹1.05 crore for unpaid digital marketing invoices. The bench found the debt above the threshold, the demand notice duly served and no dispute existing before the notice. Insolvency was admitted and an interim resolution professional appointed.

items.caseName: Ravindra Gopalkrishan Agarwal v. Jankalyan Sahakari Bank Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka & Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: Arbitral award didn't make the guarantor a co-borrower
items.text: The guarantor argued that a 2017 arbitral award imposing joint and several liability had changed his status to co-borrower. The appellate tribunal held the award only set a new mode of paying an existing liability and did not replace the guarantee. It rejected the novation arguments and upheld the Section 95 petition as within time.

items.caseName: Pankaj Chhabildas Sheth v. Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd.
items.coram: Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member) & Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
items.headline: Section 94 plea can't be used to stall SARFAESI possession
items.text: A personal guarantor filed a second Section 94 application just before the bank was to take possession of assets. The appellate tribunal found the only aim was to get the interim moratorium and block recovery. It held Section 94 protects genuine resolution efforts, not tactics to defeat secured creditors, and dismissed the appeal.

edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 25 September 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 26 September 2026

items.caseName: In the matter of Vidarbha Industries Power Limited
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) & Charanjeet Singh Gulati (Technical Member)
items.headline: Vidarbha Industries Power's merger into Adani Power sanctioned
items.text: The Mumbai bench sanctioned the amalgamation of Vidarbha Industries Power with Adani Power, one of ten group companies being folded into it. It found the scheme fair, reasonable and not contrary to law, with 1 April 2025 as the appointed date.

items.caseName: India1 Payments Limited v. Registrar of Companies
items.coram: Sunil Kumar Aggarwal (Judicial Member) & Radhakrishna Sreepada (Technical Member)
items.headline: Capital reduction approved to let an investor fund exit
items.text: The tribunal approved India1 Payments' cancellation of about 4.5 crore equity shares held by an investor fund for roughly ₹69.99 crore. The reduction was sought at the investor's request to allow a partial exit in line with SEBI directions on winding up the fund.

items.caseName: M.K. Nazar v. Indiavision Satellite Communications Limited
items.coram: Vinay Goel (Judicial Member) & Ravichandran Ramasamy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Insolvency plea against Indiavision fails: financial debt not proved
items.text: The petitioner said he advanced ₹1.5 crore to clear the company's service tax dues. The tribunal found discrepancies in the documents, no board authorisation and no bank records proving the transfer, so the financial debt was not established.

items.caseName: Aegon Shipping India Private Limited v. Commissioner of Customs (General)
items.coram: Ajay Sharma (Judicial Member) & M.M. Parthiban (Technical Member)
items.headline: No demurrage on customs-seized goods, even after 60 days
items.text: A customs cargo service provider may not charge rent or demurrage on goods seized by Customs under the Handling of Cargo in Customs Areas Regulations, 2009, whatever the 60-day recovery rule says. Suspension of the NVOCC's registration was upheld.

items.caseName: Parle Products Private Limited
items.coram: Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey (Judicial Member) & Prabhat Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Parle demerger-and-merger scheme sanctioned
items.text: The tribunal sanctioned a composite scheme demerging specified undertakings and amalgamating Parle Products with Parle Biscuits. It found the scheme fair, reasonable and not against law or public policy.

items.caseName: Small Industries Development Bank of India v. Vyshnavi Spices LLP
items.coram: Kishore Vemulapalli (Judicial Member) & Umesh Kumar Shukla (Technical Member)
items.headline: Leasehold rights in land count as the company's assets
items.text: In SIDBI's Section 7 proceedings against Vyshnavi Spices, the tribunal allowed the application and directed liquidation. It held that leasehold rights in land are to be treated as assets of the company under accounting standards.

items.caseName: State Bank of India v. Pangea Fabrics India Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) & Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: Missing postal receipt doesn't invalidate a demand notice
items.text: The corporate debtor questioned SBI's standing to enforce a corporate guarantee over an alleged default of more than ₹732 crore. The tribunal upheld SBI's locus and held that the lack of a separate postal receipt or acknowledgement does not invalidate the demand notice.

items.caseName: State Bank of India v. Suryajyoti Infotech Ltd.
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) & Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: Notice showed intent to enforce guarantee; CIRP admitted
items.text: In a Section 7 petition over a default of about ₹732 crore, the tribunal read the notice as showing the lender meant to enforce the guarantors' liability. The petition was admitted.

items.caseName: Naksh Steel Ltd. v. Auri Grow India Ltd.
items.coram: Brajendra Mani Tripathi (Judicial Member) & Man Mohan Gupta (Technical Member)
items.headline: CIRP against Auri Grow India over ₹78 crore supply dues
items.text: Auri Grow disputed the interest charged but could not deny the underlying operational debt under a Master Supply Agreement. The tribunal admitted the petition and declared a moratorium.

items.caseName: Chellanam Service Cooperative Bank v. Income Tax Officer, Non Corp Ward 2(4)
items.coram: Prashant Maharishi (Vice President) & Keshav Dubey (Judicial Member)
items.headline: Section 80P claim sent back to the AO for a fresh look
items.text: The AO had denied a primary agricultural credit society's Section 80P(2)(a)(i) deduction for want of documents without examining its accounts. The ITAT remanded the issue and gave the society 90 days to file full details.

items.caseName: Keshav Khaneja v. Mufin Green Finance Limited
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) & Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: Forensic audit ordered in Gensol–Mufin deposit dispute
items.text: The tribunal appointed an independent forensic auditor to find when Mufin adjusted Gensol Engineering's ₹1.34 crore security deposit. The answer decides whether the adjustment breached the moratorium that began on 13 June 2025.

items.caseName: The Cosmos Co-op. Bank Ltd. v. Rajendra Singhal
items.coram: Brajendra Mani Tripathi (Judicial Member) & Man Mohan Gupta (Technical Member)
items.headline: Guarantor can't escape liability for lack of personal benefit
items.text: Whether a personal guarantor gained anything from the loan is irrelevant to enforcing the guarantee. The tribunal admitted the insolvency application against the guarantor.

items.headline: IBC order affecting possession is not a landlord-tenant matter
items.text: NCLAT upheld the eviction of occupants from Venus Garments' properties through IBC proceedings, holding that the effect of an IBC order on possession does not turn the dispute into a landlord-tenant matter.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Fraudulent intent not needed to prove a preferential transaction
items.text: The effect of a transaction, not the intent behind it, decides whether it is a preferential transaction under the IBC.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Insolvency plea against Shapoorji Pallonji dismissed
items.text: The Mumbai bench declined to admit the insolvency petition against Shapoorji Pallonji.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Secured creditors must bear liquidation costs
items.text: Secured creditors who realise their security cannot avoid their share of liquidation costs by pointing to expenses that are not yet finalised.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Differential duty can be demanded without challenging self-assessment
items.text: Customs may issue a demand under Section 28 of the Customs Act for differential duty without first challenging the importer's self-assessment.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Reassessment quashed over a defective notice
items.text: A defect in the reassessment notice vitiated the proceedings against the company.

items.caseName: Combination: L'Oréal India Pvt. Ltd. / Onesto Labs Pvt. Ltd.
items.headline: CCI approves L'Oréal India's 100% acquisition of Onesto Labs
items.text: The Commission cleared the combination under the Competition Act, 2002.
